gold_trend_state.label: Trend broken
gold_trend_state.why: The long-term line is lost. BUYING now is fighting the tide - "cheap" can get much cheaper, and most big losses happen below this line. If you OWN it, this is where you require proof: SELLING into a failed bounce beats riding it lower - decide your exit line now, not after the fall resumes.

netbenefits.plain_summary: What Zacks says about the coming months, in plain language: APD goes into its next earnings report (November 5) set up to beat, not just meet - the most accurate recent estimate ($3.62) sits ABOVE the consensus ($3.60), which historically tilts the odds toward a positive surprise, and every single analyst revision in the last 60 days has been UPWARD (9 of 9 full-year estimates raised, none cut) - unusually unanimous. The year itself is expected to deliver about +11.6% earnings growth ($13.43 vs $12.03 last year), then +7.4% more in FY27, with 8.6%/yr expected over 3-5 years. The stock is not cheap for it (Forward PE 22.6, PEG 2.64, Value grade D) - you are paying a full price for a high-quality compounder, which is why Zacks rates it 2-Buy rather than Strong Buy. Last quarter fits the pattern: earnings beat on volume growth even as sales missed - margins and execution carrying the story. For your 832 shares the practical read for the coming months: hold through the November report with the surprise setup in your favor, expect the $1.81/quarter dividend (~$1,506 gross / ~$1,054 net to you) to keep arriving, and watch whether the revision wave continues - that, more than the price, is the signal these analysts are following.

regime.verdict: BULL (above the 200-day): the daily trigger alone works -- 79% hit rate, 26% of entries drew down >10%
regime.plain: regime matters more than any indicator: above the 200-day average the daily trigger alone works; below it, evidence must arm first and the trigger must come last

weekly.plain: weekly evidence on the underlying. A-D divergence was the best single component in the test (19 events, 100% positive at 60 days); RSI divergence counts when its first low was at or below 40 (<= 30 never happens on these names)

capitulation.plain: volume at least 2x its 50-day average, close in the lower third of the day near the 20-day low, then an up-day within 5 sessions. Capitulation alone in a bear worked 40% of the time; it counts only with the follow-through

band.label: owner monthly LIP support (coincides with the Oct/Nov-2025 swing lows)

support.plain: the owner band / 52-week low is a zone, not a trigger: it scores only once a weekly close is back above it (present in 70% of the good entries, but 56% alone)

volume.note: no volume on this series at TradingView
volume.plain: after a climax, a retest on shrinking volume (20-day average at 75% of the 50-day or less) is the Wyckoff "test" -- indices only; low-volume single stocks underperform

daily_divergence.plain: daily divergences were the worst input tested (69% of events down more than 10% within 60 days); shown, never scored

trigger.plain: daily trigger on the underlying: reversal candle at the 20-day low, undercut-and-reclaim, or a close above the divergence swing high with RSI above 50. In a bear it must come AFTER the evidence has armed

rule6.plain: rule 6 unchanged: a daily close below the EMA50 (or the breakout level) is a falling knife -- no averaging

KSE100.rule: Bottom Rule v2 (validated on 2021-26 IBKR bars; one real bear, ~20 confirmed events). Step 0 regime = close vs 200-day. Step 1 arm (bear only) = score >= 25 within 14 days: A-D divergence 25, RSI divergence (first low <= 40) 25, capitulation + follow-through 20, support touched + weekly close back above 15, post-climax contraction (indices) 15, daily divergence 0. Step 2 trigger = reversal at the 20-day low / undercut-reclaim / swing-high reclaim with RSI > 50. Bear: CONFIRMED only armed then triggered; PARTIAL = armed, no trigger. Bull: trigger at a higher low into the EMA20/50 band confirms. Rule 6: close below EMA50 = falling knife. KSE-100: provisional until a PSX price history is tested.

rules.1: Reversal candle at a level: low touches a support zone, closes green, above the prior day's midpoint, in the upper third of its range. Buy a tranche at the next open; the next session must hold that low or no further tranche.
rules.2: Undercut and reclaim: price trades below a prior swing low intraday but the daily close is back above it (the classic shakeout low).
rules.3: Hourly structure turns: on the 1-hour chart a higher low, then a close above the previous hourly swing high (the intraday version, for a US-session add).
rules.4: Volume signature: the low day prints at least 1.5x the 30-day average volume (capitulation), then the next session is a lighter-volume down day, or an up day on above-average volume.
rules.5: RSI with divergence: daily RSI 30-40 at the touch, and price makes a lower low while RSI makes a higher low (the strongest single signal).
rules.6: Invalidation: a daily close below the base floor breaks the base (no averaging until the next level is tested and confirms by rule 1 or 2). A close below that next level is AVOID.
